Durbin test for balanced incomplete blocks

Source: R/tests-extra.R
durbin_test.Rd

Rank-based comparison of treatments in a balanced incomplete block design (every block has k of the t treatments, every treatment appears r times): the observations are ranked within each block and the rank sums are compared (Durbin 1951). With complete blocks it is Friedman's test. Pairwise comparisons use Conover's t test on the rank sums with b k - b - t + 1 degrees of freedom; ties get average ranks.

Usage

durbin_test(
  x,
  response = NULL,
  treatment = NULL,
  block = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  p_adjust = "holm"
)

Arguments

x

An "ad_anova" object from design_anova() with one treatment factor and blocks, or a data frame.

response, treatment, block

Column names when x is a data frame; several block columns (replicate, block within replicate) are combined.

alpha

Significance level of the pairwise comparisons.

p_adjust

Adjustment of the pairwise p-values, as in stats::p.adjust(); "none" gives Conover's protected comparisons (to be read only when the overall test is significant).

Value

An object of class c("ad_durbin", "ad_nonparametric") with the test (chi-square and its F form), the pairwise comparisons, the groups with their rank sums and letters, the design parameters (design) and the least significant difference of rank sums (lsd_ranks).

References

Durbin, J. (1951). Incomplete blocks in ranking experiments. British Journal of Statistical Psychology 4, 85-90.

Conover, W. J. (1999). Practical Nonparametric Statistics, 3rd ed. Wiley, New York, section 5.9.

Examples

durbin_test(bib_sorghum, "Yield_t_ha", "Hybrid", "Block")

#> Durbin rank test for balanced incomplete blocks
#> Response: Yield_t_ha   factor: Hybrid
#> chisq = 10.44, df = 6, p = 0.1071
